SELECTED_INDEX: 4  
CONFIDENCE: 0.55  
EXPLANATION: The spectrum shows a very intense band at 1041 cm⁻¹ and another at 744 cm⁻¹. Rule GFQ-075 assigns 1040 cm⁻¹ (ν₃) and ~700 cm⁻¹ (ν₂) to an O–O–O (ozone-like) moiety; very few organic groups give such a pair of strong Raman lines. Among the candidates only molecule 4, C=CCOC(=O)OOO, contains a contiguous O–O–O segment capable of this vibration. The sharp carbonyl band at 1748 cm⁻¹ fits the ester/carbonate C=O of 4, and the strong 893 cm⁻¹ line matches the typical RO–O stretch of peroxides. Alkene C=C stretching at 1635 cm⁻¹ and C–H stretches between 2888–3098 cm⁻¹ are also consistent with the allyl fragment (C=CC). No other candidate possesses the required O₃/peroxy group, making 4 the most compatible with the observed Raman peaks.
